findings.where: Screen 3 'The emf' text, whatAmILookingAt and explain paragraph 3
findings.what: The emf is drawn as minus the flux's slope (positive from 0 to 0.5 s while the slope marker runs downhill), but nothing says so: whatAmILookingAt says the emf's height 'follows that slope' and the explain says the flux 'changes at a rate that follows sin θ' when the rate is −sin θ. Dan, fresh from Calculus (the slope of cos is −sin), will see the mismatch. Add one line saying the emf is drawn as how fast the flux falls (Faraday's minus sign; which way round counts as positive is a choice).

findings.where: interactive.ignores (and explain paragraph 4, 'close to a sine')
findings.what: These claims are true but have no quote in research-notes.md or the lesson's sources: 'Large real generators usually keep their coils still and turn the magnet', 'a real generator gets harder to turn as it supplies current' and 'their waves are close to a sine, not exactly one'. Cite each one or label it as the writer's reading.

findings.where: Screen 5 'Why a sine' against explain paragraph 3
findings.what: The screen measures the arm's θ from the upright, so its shadow is the height, cos θ, and the useful speed is vertical. The explain measures it from the floor ('across shadow', the across speed is biggest 'when the arm points straight up'). Each is right in its own frame, but the words and the picture are a quarter turn apart, and both differ from Trigonometry's habit that height is sin θ. Say once on screen that θ is measured from the upright, so here the height is cos θ, and word the explain to match the picture.
About 105 words carry two ideas: why the wave is a sine, and why it reverses at face-on. At 360 px this pushes the picture below the fold. Split it into two screens or trim it.

findings.where: Screen 10 'Three times the turns' (also screen 11), time-axis ticks
findings.what: The time axis reads '1 turn' and '2 turns', meaning turns of the coil, on the screen that asks about three times the turns of wire. Relabel the ticks, for example '1 turn round', to avoid the clash.

It says 'Why? draws the answer on the picture', but in the build Why? only shows words; the answer is drawn after a right Check. It also says the speed slider opens at 1, but screen 7 opens it at 2 turns a second. Correct the description.

'A real generator adjusts its field to hold its voltage' is backed in research-notes.md ('terminal voltage is maintained only by increasing the d.c. field current'), but that source is missing from the lesson's sources. Add it.
'The course's motor puzzle runs on this wave' refers to the course hook without restating it. Name it in a clause: the motor drawing 10 A while the wattmeter reads 1.6 kW.
'A machine with permanent magnets makes a voltage at its terminals whenever its shaft turns' follows from the lesson's rule but is not cited. Say it follows from the rule, or cite it.

The emf scale jumps from 4 V full scale (screens 3 to 6) to 16 V, so the same 3.14 V wave looks a quarter as tall. The emf axis shows only 0, so nothing marks the change apart from the dashed ghost. Add one value tick on the emf axis.

findings.where: Screen 2 (edge-on coil, 360 px light and dark)
findings.what: Edge-on, the coil's wires (x 38 and 118, radius 7.5) touch the pole faces, the right wire covers the middle field line's arrowhead, and the 'N' crowds the left wire. Bring the coil in a little (RC about 36) or move the poles out.

findings.where: Coil screens with the lamp (3 to 7, 9, 11)
findings.what: The lamp never brightens, and while |sin θ| is below about 0.18 the label reads 'current' with no arrow drawn. Make the lamp glow with |emf| so it shows the current, and hide the label when the arrow is too short to draw.

'Each emf is worked out from the coil's turns of wire, field, area and turns a second' is not true on screens 10 to 12, whose peaks (12 V, 20 V, 100 V) are given as example figures. Reword it to cover them.
